nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be odd and not prime, and let $s$ be a natural number. Among the $(n - 1)^s$ lists $(b_1, \dots, b_s)$ of bases with $0 < b_i < n$, at most $\lfloor (n - 1)/4 \rfloor^s$ make the Miller–Rabin test of $n$ with bases $b_1, \dots, b_s$ answer *prime*.
nodes.title: Quarter error bound for Miller–Rabin with several bases

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be odd and not prime, and let $s$ be a natural number. Among the $(n - 1)^s$ lists $(b_1, \dots, b_s)$ of bases with $0 < b_i < n$, at most $((n - 1)/2)^s$ make the Miller–Rabin test of $n$ with bases $b_1, \dots, b_s$ answer *prime*.
nodes.title: Half error bound for Miller–Rabin with several bases

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a Carmichael number: $n > 2$, $n$ is not prime, and $b^{n-1} \equiv 1 \pmod n$ for every $b$ coprime to $n$. Then at most $(n - 1)/2$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$.
nodes.title: At most half the bases are non-witnesses for a Carmichael number

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$, and suppose some $x$ coprime to $n$ has $x^{n-1} \not\equiv 1 \pmod n$. Then at most $(n - 1)/2$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$.
nodes.title: At most half the bases are non-witnesses when some unit fails Fermat's test

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a Carmichael number: $n > 2$, $n$ is not prime, and $b^{n-1} \equiv 1 \pmod n$ for every $b$ coprime to $n$. Then at most $(n - 1)/4$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$.
nodes.title: At most a quarter of the bases are non-witnesses for a Carmichael number

nodes.summary: At most a quarter of the bases are non-witnesses when some unit fails Fermat's test and the modulus is not a prime power. Let $n > 1$ be odd and not prime, and not of the form $p^e$ with $p$ prime and $e \ge 2$. Suppose some $z$ coprime to $n$ has $z^{n-1} \not\equiv 1 \pmod n$. Then at most $(n - 1)/4$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$.
nodes.title: At most a quarter of the bases are non-witnesses when some unit fails Fermat's test and the modulus is not a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $k \ge 2$ with $p^k$ odd. Then at most $(p^k - 1)/4$ of the bases $1, \dots, p^k - 1$ are non-witnesses for $p^k$.
nodes.title: At most a quarter of the bases are non-witnesses for an odd prime power

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be odd and not prime. Then at most $(n - 1)/4$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$, so one uniformly random base fails to expose $n$ as composite with probability at most $1/4$.
nodes.title: At most a quarter of the bases are non-witnesses

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be odd and not prime. Then at most $(n - 1)/2$ of the bases $1, \dots, n - 1$ are non-witnesses for $n$; equivalently, at least $(n - 1)/2$ of them are witnesses to the compositeness of $n$.
nodes.title: At most half the bases are non-witnesses

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ and let $a$ be a natural number such that the witness test $\mathrm{WITNESS}(a, n)$ returns false. Then $a^{n-1} \equiv 1 \pmod n$ and $a$ is coprime to $n$.
nodes.title: Non-witnesses pass Fermat's test and are units

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list of bases, the Miller–Rabin test on $n$ with these bases answers *prime* if and only if, for every base $a$ in the list, the witness test $\mathrm{WITNESS}(a, n)$ returns false, that is, $a$ is not a witness to the compositeness of $n$.
nodes.title: Miller–Rabin answers prime exactly when no base is a witness

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a prime. For every list of bases $a_1, \dots, a_s$ (possibly empty) with $0 < a_i < n$ for each $i$, the Miller–Rabin test run on $n$ with these bases answers *prime*.
nodes.title: The Miller–Rabin test never rejects a prime when its bases lie in range

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$ and a list of bases $a_1, \dots, a_s$, the test runs the witness test for $n$ on each base in turn. It answers *composite* as soon as some base $a_i$ is a witness to the compositeness of $n$, and *prime* if none is (in particular on the empty list). Its cost is the sum of the costs of the witness tests it runs.
nodes.title: The Miller–Rabin test

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the non-witnesses of $n$ form the finite set of bases $a$ with $0 < a < n$ for which the Miller–Rabin witness test $\mathrm{WITNESS}(a, n)$ returns false, that is, the bases that do not witness the compositeness of $n$.
nodes.title: Non-witnesses of a number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $a_1, \dots, a_s$ a list of bases with $0 < a_i < n$ for each $i$. If the Miller–Rabin test run on $n$ with these bases answers *composite*, then $n$ is not prime.
nodes.title: With bases in range, a composite answer of the Miller–Rabin test is correct

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $0 < a < n$. If the witness test reports $a$ as a witness to the compositeness of $n$, then $n$ is not prime.
nodes.title: A Miller–Rabin witness in range proves compositeness

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m > 0$, the two-adic split of $m$ is the pair $(t, u)$ of natural numbers with $m = 2^t u$ and $u$ odd. For $m = 0$ it is $(0, 0)$.
nodes.title: Splitting off the power of two

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ and write $n - 1 = 2^t u$ with $u$ odd. If $a$ is a natural number for which the Miller–Rabin witness test $\mathrm{WITNESS}(a, n)$ returns false, then $a^u \equiv 1 \pmod n$, or $a^{2^i u} \equiv -1 \pmod n$ for some $i < t$.
nodes.title: What a non-witness satisfies

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a prime and $a$ a natural number with $0 < a < n$. Then the witness test does not report $a$ as a witness to the compositeness of $n$.
nodes.title: A prime has no Miller–Rabin witnesses in range

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $x$ be natural numbers with $x < n$. If the Miller–Rabin squaring loop modulo $n$, started at $x$ with $k$ squarings to perform, reports no witness, then $x = 1$ or $x^{2^i} \equiv -1 \pmod n$ for some $i < k$.
nodes.title: When the squaring loop finds no witness

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $k$ and $x$ be natural numbers with $x < p$ and $x^{2^k} \bmod p = 1$. Then the squaring loop modulo $p$ started at $x$ with $k$ squarings remaining reports no witness.
nodes.title: The squaring loop modulo a prime finds no witness when it ends at 1

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $x$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, $x < n$ and $x^{2^k} \bmod n \ne 1$. Then the squaring loop modulo $n$ started at $x$ with $k$ squarings remaining reports a witness.
nodes.title: The squaring loop reports a witness when it does not end at 1

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $x$, the cost of the squaring loop modulo $n$ started at $x$ with $k$ squarings remaining is at most $k$.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the Miller–Rabin squaring loop

nodes.summary:
Fix a modulus $n$. With no squarings remaining, the loop at the current value $x$ reports a witness exactly when $x 
e 1$, at no cost. With $k + 1$ squarings remaining, it costs one modular multiplication and computes $y = x^2  mod n$; it reports a witness if $y = 1$, $x 
e 1$ and $x 
e n - 1$, and otherwise continues at $y$ with $k$ squarings remaining.
nodes.title: The Miller–Rabin squaring loop

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 1$. If $a^{n-1} \bmod n \ne 1$, that is, $a^{n-1} \not\equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, then the Miller–Rabin witness test on base $a$ and modulus $n$ returns true.
nodes.title: Fermat witnesses are Miller–Rabin witnesses

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, write $n - 1 = 2^t u$ with $u$ odd (here $n - 1$ is truncated at $0$, and $t = u = 0$ when $n \le 1$). The cost of the witness test on base $a$ and modulus $n$ is at most the cost of the modular exponentiation of $a$ to the power $u$ modulo $n$ plus $t$: at most one multiplication for each of the $t$ squarings.
nodes.title: Cost of the Miller–Rabin witness test

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, write $n - 1 = 2^t u$ with $u$ odd (here $n - 1$ is truncated at $0$, and $t = u = 0$ when $n \le 1$). The test sets $x_0$ to the result of modular exponentiation of $a$ to the power $u$ modulo $n$, which is $a^u \bmod n$ when $u > 0$ and $1$ when $u = 0$. For $i = 1, \dots, t$ it computes $x_i = x_{i-1}^2 \bmod n$ and returns true as soon as $x_i = 1$, $x_{i-1} \ne 1$ and…
nodes.title: Miller–Rabin witness test

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
